title: Sell Mineral Rights in Houston, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Houston, PA
metaDescription: Own mineral rights in or near Houston, Washington County? Core Marcellus wet-gas territory with heavy Range Resources drilling. We buy — no pressure, just numbers.
heroLead: Houston, Pennsylvania sits along Chartiers Creek in the busiest stretch of Washington County's Marcellus development, and most families here have owned a lease longer than they've thought hard about it.
intro: Houston is a small Washington County borough along Chartiers Creek, named for an early landowner rather than the Texas city, and it sits right in the middle of the county's wet-gas Marcellus core. Range Resources and other operators have drilled this area heavily for over a decade, so Houston-area families are more likely than most in Pennsylvania to have real production history to look at.
We buy mineral and royalty interests in and around Houston, whether you're holding a strong-producing interest, one that's declined significantly, or a fractional share split among heirs.

sections.heading: One of Washington County's busiest corridors
paragraphs: This stretch along Chartiers Creek has been developed early and thoroughly, which means most Houston-area tracts are past the initial production spike and into a more predictable decline pattern — useful information for valuing an interest accurately.

sections.heading: What decline curves tell us about value
paragraphs: A well several years into production tells a very different value story than a newly turned-in-line well. We look at where a specific well sits on its decline curve, not only whether it's producing at all.

sections.heading: Deductions on a mature Houston-area lease
paragraphs: Older, mature leases in this corridor often carry the same post-production deduction structures that frustrate owners countywide — gathering, compression, and dehydration charges netted out before royalty is paid, allowed under Pennsylvania's Guaranteed Minimum Royalty Act floor but not eliminated by it.
We read the specific royalty clause in your lease rather than assuming a standard deduction structure applies, since terms vary even within this corridor.

faqs.question: Is Houston, PA related to Houston, Texas?
faqs.answer: No, the borough is named for an early local landowner, unrelated to the Texas city, though the coincidence comes up often when people search for it.

faqs.question: How does a well's decline curve affect what my Houston-area interest is worth?
faqs.answer: A well later in its decline typically produces less than it did early on, which affects both current royalty income and the value of the underlying interest — we look at the actual production trend rather than early peak numbers.

faqs.question: My Houston-area royalty checks have shrunk over the years even with the same lease. Why?
faqs.answer: This is usually a combination of natural well decline and post-production deductions, both common in this mature, heavily developed part of Washington County.

faqs.question: Would selling my Houston-area royalty interest affect my ability to receive future lease bonus payments?
faqs.answer: Selling a producing royalty interest typically transfers future royalty income to the buyer; whether it affects any separate bonus provisions depends on the specific lease and what exactly is being sold, which we'll walk through with you.
